The tags$head goes in the UI itself, alongside your controls or whatever. It almost doesn't matter where you put it, it'll get promoted to the <head> of the document when it's rendered.

The theme argument would go onto fluidPage, navbarPage, or whatever you're using to enclose your UI.

messages.subject: Re: Can't update multiple radio buttons at once
messages.subject_clean: Can't update multiple radio buttons at once
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

a minimal working example would have been nice. If you replace "character(0)" by one of your choices then it works. I guess what you want to do is to return to the "not anything selected" state. Please read the Details section in the documentation to radioButtons: http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/radioButtons.html

Best Sigbert

library(shiny)

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
          radioButtons(label="raceId",

                       inputId = "raceId",
                       choices=list("White", "Black","Unidentified"),

                       selected=character(0)),
          radioButtons(label= "genderId",

                       inputId = "genderId",
                       choices=list("Male", "Female", "Unidentified"),

                       selected=character(0)),
          actionButton(inputId = "Submit",                                      label="Submit")),
      mainPanel(
         plotOutput("distPlot")
      )
   )
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    observe({
        str(input$Submit)

        updateRadioButtons(session=session,                                        inputId = "raceId",

                           selected="White")

        updateRadioButtons(session=session,                                        inputId = "genderId",

                           selected="Male")
    })#end observe event
})

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Dear all,
I have being trying to display pdf documents within an iframe at a tabset within the main panel based on selectInput selections.

At the server side the input selection construct in a reactive manner the folder directory and document name.

Any guidance is appreciated.

Thanks!

library(shiny)

ui <- # Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
headerPanel("Test Show Pdf"),
sidebarPanel(
selectInput("Year", "Choose a Year:",
choices = c("2012", "2011")),
selectInput("Folder", "Choose a Folder:",

mainPanel(
tabsetPanel(type = "tabs",
tabPanel("Outcome Reports", htmlOutput("viewReport"))), width = 10)
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {
# Main path to Reports

filePutReport <- reactive(
paste(MainPathReport, input$Folder, input$Year, "/",

)

output$viewReport <- renderText({
return(

})
})

Eek, I think that actually posted this in the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> group.  So my apologies for that.

Anyways, we have about 4 levels of reactivity for each of our data tables or plots -- raw data -> filtered data -> grouped data -> formatted data.  This makes it really easy for us to use the same grouped data in multiple different formats without having to reprocess all of the data each time a user makes a change to the settings.

But the problem is, we either show progress on only one reactive expression, or we show 4 times the progress bars.  I would like to consolidate this into one single progress bar each time one of the "formatted data" reactive data is updated, and allow all of the sub-reactive data to update that progress bar as they provide their data.

Hopefully that makes sense.

I've tried the examples using Progress and withProgress, but we need to be using multiple reactive data to be as flexible with the processing as we can get for multiple uses, instead of a whole bunch of single reactive with multiple functions.

Has anyone done anything like this before?  Any suggestions?  Any help will be greatly appreciated.  Much thanks everyone.
~Laz Peterson

messages.subject: shiny on rhel 6 with odbc to oracle db on other server - environment variables for spawned R-process
messages.subject_clean: shiny on rhel 6 with odbc to oracle db on other server - environment variables for spawned R-process
messages.body_plain:
>
I just spend a lot of time solving the following problem.
As a total noob in Linux, shiny and R I hope this will help someone in the future.

I installed oracle-instant-client to create an odbc connection from my RHEL 6 server to my database server

To make the connection possible from within R I had to set the following

LD_LIBRARY_PATH
TWO_TASK
ODBCINIT
ODBCSYSINIT
After that i could successfully connect to the database from a interactive R-session that i start as root !!
But when i tried the odb-connection through my shiny-server, I got the following message:

> Warning in RODBC::odbcDriverConnect("DSN=<server>;UID=<uid>;PWD=<pwd>") :
>   [RODBC] ERROR: state IM002, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Data source name not found, and no default driver specified
> Warning in RODBC::odbcDriverConnect("DSN=<server>;UID=<uid>;PWD=<pwd>") :
>   ODBC connection failed

These were the exact same messages  i got in my interactive R-session before i had the ODBCINIT and ODBCSYSINIT set.

When i checked the environment for the shiny-server and the spawned R-processes i could indeed see that none of the variables were set:

ps aux | grep shiny-server
strings /proc/<pid>/environ
ps aux | grep R
strings /proc/<pid>/environ
NOTE: i could clearly see that are processes were running as root
NOTE: the LD_LIBRARY_PATH was filled with R- and java-library locations (both for shiny-server and the R-processes) but no libraries for Oracle

Possible solution 1:
According to the administrator manual for shiny-server (1.4.2), the shiny-server (when spawning the R-processes) would first read /etc/profile and then the ~/.bash-profile of the 'run_as' user  as set in /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
In my case it was set globally to 'run_as root;'

I added the environment variables to the .bash-profile for root, restarted my shiny-server (just to be sure), but this did not make any difference.
NOK - Using the commands (see above) i could see no difference in any of the variables for either the shiny-server or the spawned R-processes

Possible solution 2:
According to some older threats (beginning 2014) LD_LIBRARY_PATH could be set / extended in /etc/init/shiny-server.conf by way of the 'env' command: env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<lib>
NOTE: i discovered that depending on the location in the (upstart)script the character expansion does not work. So  env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<lib>:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH  was no option.

I added the statements for all the environment variables and then rebooted my server.
NOK - Using the commands (see above) I could now see that for the shiny-server process all the environment variables were correctly set, but for the spawned R-processes till not !!

Possible solution 3:
Add all the settings to the /etc/environment
NOTE: you are not supposed to use the export statement then, so just TWO_TASK=<value> and then a new line forevery setting

I added for all the environment variables and then rebooted my server.
NOK -Using the commands (see above) i could see no difference in any of the variables for either the shiny-server or the spawned R-processes

Possible solution 4:
Find out where the initial settings for the LD_LIBRARY_PATH were made that i could see when checking the environment for the spawned R-processes

> grep -rl LD_LIBRARY_PATH= /usr/lib64/R

among others this resulted in:
/usr/lib64/R/etc/ldpaths
/usr/lib64/R/etc/javaconf
In the same library i also found Makeconf

In ldpaths i could see that the LD_LIBRARY_PATH was set to R_LD_LIBRARY_PATH after a check if LD_LIBRARY_PATH was empty.
So before this check i added:

> LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/oracle/12.1/client64/lib

in Makeconf i set and exported the other variables

TWO_TASK
ODBCINIT
ODBCSYSINIT

OK - i restarted my shiny-server and now my odbc-connection worked from within the spawned R-processes.

Questions:

- Why doesn't my shiny-server make use of the /etc/profile as stated in the admin manual?
- Is the solution i finally arrived at, an accepted one, or is there another better one?

I spend a good 20 hours googling and solving this problem, so thanks to all of you who ever made a posting on any of the many problems I stumbled across :):)

Jasper Drop

messages.subject: shiny app only works on specific browsers / platforms
messages.subject_clean: shiny app only works on specific browsers / platforms
messages.body_plain:
I have programmed a shiny app in RStudio using R version 3.2.4. The app can be found here: https://koenvandenberge.shinyapps.io/tempConditioning/ Note that there is quite a lot of data to be loaded so it takes a couple of seconds to load.

I have also tried deploying it fro Mac aswell as from Windows - nothing changes.

I have deployed it on my Macbook and it seems as if it only works on Safari and Chromium browsers. It does not seem to work on Chrome or Firefox browsers. With this I mean that the plots which should be generated are not. The drop-down menu is present as it should be, so the app does not crash, but the plots that should be generated by selecting something from the drop-down menu do not.

Is there any way to fix this? You can find the code of my app below:
library(shiny)
library(scales)
load("countMatrix.RData")
countMatrixAllSub = as.data.frame(countMatrix$counts[,-1]) ; rm(countMatrix)
sampleNames = unlist(lapply(strsplit(colnames(countMatrixAllSub),split=".",fixed=TRUE), function(x) x[4]))
sampleNames[28] <- "3c0a"
treat=substr(sampleNames,2,2)
time=substr(sampleNames,3,nchar(sampleNames)-1)
timeC=as.numeric(time)
timeC[timeC==15]=0.25

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

   # Application title
   titlePanel("Gene expression: conditioning experiment Gust"),

   # Sidebar with a
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         selectInput("gene",
                     "Pick a gene",
                      choices = rownames(countMatrixAllSub))
      ),

      # Show a plot of the generated distribution
      mainPanel(
         plotOutput("genePlot")
      )
   )
))

# Define server logic required to draw an expression plot
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$genePlot <- renderPlot({
    par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 3, 1))
    plot(y=countMatrixAllSub[input$gene,],x=timeC, col=c("black","red")[as.numeric(factor(treat))], pch=19,cex=.6,xaxt="n",xlab="Time", ylab="Expression")
    lines(x=unique(timeC[!timeC==0]),y=colMeans(sapply(unique(timeC[!timeC==0]), function(t) as.matrix(countMatrixAllSub[input$gene,treat=="c" & timeC==t]))), col=1)
    lines(x=unique(timeC[!timeC==0]),y=colMeans(sapply(unique(timeC[!timeC==0]), function(t) as.matrix(countMatrixAllSub[input$gene,treat=="t" & timeC==t]))), col=2)
    axis(1,at=c(0,0.25,1,3,6,9),labels=c("","15m","1h","3h","6h","9h"))
    abline(v=c(0,0.25,1,3,6,9),col=alpha("grey",.6))
    mtext("Conditioned",side=3, adj=0,col="red")
    mtext("Unconditioned",side=3, adj=0.2, col="black")
  })
})

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

I'm trying to modularize my shiny map apps so that I can build dashboards that have lots of functionality but are also maintainable and robust. I'd say that my understanding of reactive programming is intermediate (at best) and I have no prior experience using these modular patterns, so this task has been challenging thus far.

I noticed that when I include `leafletProxy()` (triggered by an observer) within the server logic of a module, that the `id` argument does not reflect the module's `id` (as set by NS). Why is this the case? And is my work-around solution (to pass a second copy to a NS function inside the module's server logic - see the gist below) the recommended way to solve this problem?

Here's a gist with a reproducible example of the problem and my solution: https://gist.github.com/tiernanmartin/f78cf4ffb1e488d643afb6d43c775536

Thanks for your feedback,

Tiernan

messages.subject: Re: RenderUI not updating?
messages.subject_clean: RenderUI not updating?
messages.body_plain:
gene_info and autocomplete_list are regular variables--Shiny can't detect changes in them. You could theoretically call makeReactiveBinding for each of them to magically make them reactive values (or make them into members of a reactiveValues object). But in this case, that's not what you want to do. Instead, change each one of the to a reactive(...) expression--you don't need observe(...) at all here. messages.body_plain:
Hi,

As part of a project I'm working on, I need to render different versions of a shiny application based on the logged in user (using PAM auth). The way I do this is slightly convoluted, but seems to work well enough. I've described it below:

1) User logs in through PAM auth

2) Username is retrieved through session$user and assigned to currentUser
currentUser <- session$user

3) currentUser is used to retrieve a list of numbers from a lookup table, each one representing a UI element.
Example of lookup table:

dashboardConfig.csv
username ui1 ui2 ui3 ui4 ui5 ui6 ....
Test          2    5    1    6    4    3    ....

4) These numbers retrieve a particular function (held in a list called funcList) which builds the appropriate UI element in the appropriate place. Below is an example of the generic/user agnostic UI script and the generic/user agnostic server script

UI snippet:

fluidRow(
         uiOutput("row1pos1"),
         uiOutput("row1pos2"),
         uiOutput("row1pos3"),
         uiOutput("row1pos4")
)
etc.

Server snippet:

  output$row1pos1 <- renderUI({
    funcList[[dashboardConfig$ui1[dashboardConfig$username==currentUser]]](input,output)
  })

  output$row1pos2 <- renderUI({
    funcList[[dashboardConfig$ui2[dashboardConfig$username==currentUser]]](input,output)
  })

  output$row1pos3 <- renderUI({
    funcList[[dashboardConfig$ui3[dashboardConfig$username==currentUser]]](input,output)
  })

  output$row1pos4 <- renderUI({
    funcList[[dashboardConfig$ui4[dashboardConfig$username==currentUser]]](input,output)
  })
etc.

Here is an example function:

  fn13= function(input,output){
    box(id = "top5", title = "Top 5",status = "info",solidHeader = TRUE,width = 6,
        DT::renderDataTable(
        ....
        ....
    )
  }

This function will render a data table inside a box as intended.

My problem is that the only case so far where this doesn't work is when I try to put a ggvis output inside a box in the one function (similar to above). The ggvis is output fine, but there is no sign of the box. I have very little understanding of how all this compiles and I've only recently discovered ggvis, so I'm not entirely sure what's going on. The issue is that I can't hard-code a box and then put the ggvis plot inside it because not all users will want to see that ggvis plot, and if the box is hard-coded within the UI, it will appear for all users, and hence make this whole application "non-user agnostic".

Is there a way to make a ggvis output appear in a box using just one function?

This is what the ggvis function looks like:

fn10 = function(input,output){
     box(id = "spendByWeek", title = paste("Spend by week",sep=""),status = "primary",solidHeader = TRUE,width = 6,
      data(input,output) %>% as.data.frame() %>% mutate(WEEK_NUMBER= as.numeric(WEEK_NO)) %>%
      ggvis(x = ~ WEEK_NUMBER, y = ~ SPEND ) %>%
      set_options("row2pos3",height=420,width="auto") %>%
      bind_shiny("row2pos3ggvis","row2pos3")
     )
},

Any guidance would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks a lot,
Sam

messages.body_plain:
Hi Winston,
I've been trying to use the newly implemented save function which works great!
However, when an observeEvent is triggered by pressing an actionButton, it is also triggered by the session restore.

library(shiny)

ui = function(request) {
  fluidPage(
    uiOutput("showTest"),
    bookmarkButton()
  )
}
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$showTest <- renderUI({
    actionButton("test", "hi")
  })

  observeEvent(input$test,{
    print('hello')
  })
})

enableBookmarking(store = "url")
shinyApp(ui, server)

The reason is that the value (number of click) is recorded and then restored.You certainly have a reason for programming it like that, but maybe you should give the user the possibility not to save the value of actionButton input? (I guess that many people use actionButtons to trigger an event and are not interested by the input value).
Best regards.

We're still thinking about some of these issues, but one thing that can be assumed is that a given pool instance will only hand out connections that are exactly equivalent to each other. So that means that if you have multiple DB users that will be chosen according to who is logged in, you'll need to have a pool not at the process level, but have a separate pool for each session probably (and remember to close the pool when the session ends (?onSessionEnded)). But how to actually get the DB password for each user into there is still an open question.

Basically you can think of each pool being tied to a specific set of dbConnect arguments, no more or less than that.

On Sat, Sep 10, 2016 at 2:30 PM Enzo <emart...@gmail.com> wrote:

> First of all, congrats for developing pool!
>
> It was really something missing in shiny more complex applications.
>
> While I understand the package is still very new, I wonder if you could give some anticipation on how you plan to handle:
>
> - multiple DB user & shiny users (in case of Shiny Server Pro)
> - multiple roles with different rights
> - different schemas (e.g for PostgreSQL), possibly associated to different roles / users
>
> In my mind the question is whether users / roles and possibly schemas are part of a pool, i.e. specified once for a particular pool definition once-per-connection-pool, or some of the above will still need to be specified every time within a pool.
>
> Thanks Enzo
>
>

messages.subject_clean: Window size when using shinydashboard
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am using the library shinydashboard to customize my shiny apps.
When I run the app, the plot and modules open in another window with a size defined at 611px height (in the code of the dashboard funtion).
After that, when I publish my app on the web, if the plots are smaller than the window opened, then the big white space under the plots is also published (you can see an example here : http://www.atlasmontblanc.org/fr/reproduction-des-mesanges).
I tried to change the "min-height:611px" in the code of the dashboard function, it works when I increase it, but it does not work when I decrease the number.

I don't have this problem when I don't use the dashboard package.

Consequently, I wanted to know if somebody had a solution to decrease the size of the window that opens when we run the app, or a solution to make the white space not appearing.

Here is a code (ui.R) that I use:
body <- dashboardBody(
  fluidRow(
    box(width=5, height="350px", leafletOutput("mymap", height="325px"), solidHeader = F,
        status="warning"),
    box(width=7, status="warning", solidHeader = F,
        selectInput("variable2016", "Variable - 2016", vars1, width="200px"),
        plotOutput("hist2016", height=250))
    )
)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(disable=T),
  dashboardSidebar(disable=T),
  body)

Thanks a lot
Cheers

Marjorie

messages.subject: Re: shiny on rhel 6 with odbc to oracle db on other server - environment variables for spawned R-process
messages.subject_clean: shiny on rhel 6 with odbc to oracle db on other server - environment variables for spawned R-process
messages.body_plain:
Not sure if this is the type of answer you were looking for... In my experience there are two methods that work very well without any of the fuss of setting up the oracle OCI...

Option #1: Set up pool connections with the new pool package, after installing ROracle (you should be able to specify the connection with something along these lines) (preferred)
library(DBI)
library(pool)
library(ROracle)

drv <- dbDriver("Oracle")

    pool <- dbPool(drv,
                   username = "username"
                   password = "passwd",
                   dbname = "(DESCRIPTION =
                         (ADDRESS =
                         (PROTOCOL = TCP)
                           (HOST = xxxxx)
                           (PORT = xxxx)
                         )
                         (CONNECT_DATA =
                           (SERVICE_NAME = servname)
                           ))"
)

Option #2: Use RJDBC to set up the connection through rJava.

Best,
LG

On Tuesday, September 6, 2016 at 3:57:23 AM UTC-4, Jasper Drop wrote:
> >
> I just spend a lot of time solving the following problem.
> As a total noob in Linux, shiny and R I hope this will help someone in the future.
>
>
> I installed oracle-instant-client to create an odbc connection from my RHEL 6 server to my database server
>
> To make the connection possible from within R I had to set the following
>
> LD_LIBRARY_PATH
> TWO_TASK
> ODBCINIT
> ODBCSYSINIT
> After that i could successfully connect to the database from a interactive R-session that i start as root !!
> But when i tried the odb-connection through my shiny-server, I got the following message:
>
> > Warning in RODBC::odbcDriverConnect("DSN=<server>;UID=<uid>;PWD=<pwd>") :
> >   [RODBC] ERROR: state IM002, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Data source name not found, and no default driver specified
> > Warning in RODBC::odbcDriverConnect("DSN=<server>;UID=<uid>;PWD=<pwd>") :
> >   ODBC connection failed
>
> These were the exact same messages  i got in my interactive R-session before i had the ODBCINIT and ODBCSYSINIT set.
>
> When i checked the environment for the shiny-server and the spawned R-processes i could indeed see that none of the variables were set:
>
> ps aux | grep shiny-server
> strings /proc/<pid>/environ
> ps aux | grep R
> strings /proc/<pid>/environ
> NOTE: i could clearly see that are processes were running as root
> NOTE: the LD_LIBRARY_PATH was filled with R- and java-library locations (both for shiny-server and the R-processes) but no libraries for Oracle
>
> Possible solution 1:
> According to the administrator manual for shiny-server (1.4.2), the shiny-server (when spawning the R-processes) would first read /etc/profile and then the ~/.bash-profile of the 'run_as' user  as set in /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
> In my case it was set globally to 'run_as root;'
>
> I added the environment variables to the .bash-profile for root, restarted my shiny-server (just to be sure), but this did not make any difference.
> NOK - Using the commands (see above) i could see no difference in any of the variables for either the shiny-server or the spawned R-processes
>
> Possible solution 2:
> According to some older threats (beginning 2014) LD_LIBRARY_PATH could be set / extended in /etc/init/shiny-server.conf by way of the 'env' command: env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<lib>
> NOTE: i discovered that depending on the location in the (upstart)script the character expansion does not work. So  env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<lib>:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH  was no option.
>
> I added the statements for all the environment variables and then rebooted my server.
> NOK - Using the commands (see above) I could now see that for the shiny-server process all the environment variables were correctly set, but for the spawned R-processes till not !!
>
> Possible solution 3:
> Add all the settings to the /etc/environment
> NOTE: you are not supposed to use the export statement then, so just TWO_TASK=<value> and then a new line forevery setting
>
> I added for all the environment variables and then rebooted my server.
> NOK -Using the commands (see above) i could see no difference in any of the variables for either the shiny-server or the spawned R-processes
>
> Possible solution 4:
> Find out where the initial settings for the LD_LIBRARY_PATH were made that i could see when checking the environment for the spawned R-processes
>
> > grep -rl LD_LIBRARY_PATH= /usr/lib64/R
>
> among others this resulted in:
> /usr/lib64/R/etc/ldpaths
> /usr/lib64/R/etc/javaconf
> In the same library i also found Makeconf
>
> In ldpaths i could see that the LD_LIBRARY_PATH was set to R_LD_LIBRARY_PATH after a check if LD_LIBRARY_PATH was empty.
> So before this check i added:
>
> > LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/oracle/12.1/client64/lib
>
> in Makeconf i set and exported the other variables
>
> TWO_TASK
> ODBCINIT
> ODBCSYSINIT
>
> OK - i restarted my shiny-server and now my odbc-connection worked from within the spawned R-processes.
>
>
> Questions:
>
> - Why doesn't my shiny-server make use of the /etc/profile as stated in the admin manual?
> - Is the solution i finally arrived at, an accepted one, or is there another better one?

messages.subject: Fixing Shiny Server's static file (CSS, JS) cache thwarting
messages.subject_clean: Fixing Shiny Server's static file (CSS, JS) cache thwarting
messages.body_plain:
I've got a number of Shiny apps that all tend to use the same Shiny-related packages and their associated CSS and JS static files.  As far as I can tell from looking at HTTP requests, Shiny Server seems to prevent to use of browser caching for these, quite numerous and sometimes large, CSS and JS static files.  So, every app load/switch requires them to be re-downloaded, again and again.  It's probably the single-largest source of inefficiency and slow app load times for my Shiny apps.

So, to combat this, I've started using suppressDependencies() to prevent Shiny-related packages from emitting <link ...> and <script ...> tags and replaced them with my own <link ...> and <script ...> tags that fetch the same static CSS and JS files either from a content delivery network or from my own NGINX server (which does not thwart caching of CSS and JS).   (I noticed that the Shiny Server alternative from statsplot.com <http://statsplot.com> which helps address this issue for core Shiny JS and CSS under the <app_name>/shared/ directory seems now to be unavailable.  So I've been seeking alternative fixes to this problem.)

Has anyone else been dealing with this performance issue around non-caching of static CSS and JS files?  Have you been dealing with it using suppressDependencies() or any other means?

I'm not really happy with this kludgy hack (and the perpetual extra maintenance now required with every package version change), so I'm really open to any ideas others might have about this.

TIA,

Joel

messages.body_plain:
Hey there Daniel,

Not sure if this will give you any insight to solving your issue, but one suggestion could be to use renderUI/uiOutput to create your selectInput dynamically, and then observeEvent for any changes to either of those selectInput to save the selected value into a reactiveValues that can be read to set the value when using uiOutput.

If the reactiveValues item for that input is NULL, then it just doesn't create any selected value.  Of course, if the user had selected a value, when uiOutput goes to put together the selectInput on any tabPanel, it will pre-set that previously selected value.

We have a couple things like this in our apps, a little bit different than your intended function though.

Just a thought ... Hope it helps.

~Laz

messages.subject_clean: Shiny datatable issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

We are using a series of datatables(DT::dataTableOutput) on a single page. The data contents are linked to the row selected in another table (on the same page) and is fetched from the database dynamically.

For e.g. There are total 3 tables on the screen.

Table1’s data is independent.

Table2’s data is dependent on the row selected in Table1.

Table3’s data is dependent on the row selected in Table2.

So the dependant datatable is refreshed every time there is a change in row selection. We have noticed that the tables get strolled quite a few times, and the data is not refreshed as per the selection. I have added some logging messages and it shows that the row selection works fine (I can always see correct details for selected row), but the table data does not refresh accordingly. There is no specific pattern we have noticed for this behaviour.

Since the table data shows important details about the activity performed at backend, this behaviour shows wrong information to the users and affects their further actions.

It would be great if you can help us to fix this issue.

Regards,
Manali

Hello all,

Thanks for taking a look. My name is Ken Steif. I am the Director of the Masters of Urban Spatial Analytics <http://www.design.upenn.edu/all-degrees-certificates/musa> program at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. We combine spatial analysis and traditional data science techniques in the urban planning domain.

We are working to bolster our data visualization offerings - particularly dynamic, web-based visualization including maps and dashboards. We currently teach Carto, Leaflet, ArcServer and associated languages. Most analytical classes however employ R and thus, Shiny is a natural extension.

We are looking for someone to teach 4-5 classes this spring on Shiny as part of a course that will include unstructured data retrieval and visualization.

If you are interested, we'd love to see a portfolio and perhaps a CV. Teaching experience would be great but a track record of communicating technology solutions is good too.

If you are interested, I'd love to chat. Please respond with an email and I'll be in touch.

Ken Steif, PhD

messages.body_plain:
1) The definition of dat2 should go outside of the renderPlot--it should be at the same level of indentation as "output$hist1 <- renderPlot({".
2) You're creating the plot1 object, but you're neither returning it nor printing it. Any of these would work:

output$hist1 <- renderPlot({
  ggplot(...) + ...
})

output$hist1 <- renderPlot({
  plot1 <- ggplot(...) + ...
  plot1
})

output$hist1 <- renderPlot({
  plot1 <- ggplot(...) + ...
  print(plot1)
})

But not this:

output$hist1 <- renderPlot({
  plot1 <- ggplot(...) + ...
})

messages.body_plain:
Dear Folks--
A couple of months ago I ran across a web page that displayed a kind of map, made with shiny, that I have wanted to make for a long time. I wrote down the URL, and then promptly lost it. Since then I have spent many hours googling around looking for it. I will describe it, and hope that you can tell me where to find model code.

The map was a variety of non-contiguous cartogram. Actually a combined cartogram and choropleth, but the cartogram part is what I do not know how to do.It was not a rectangular or Dorling cartogram, but a cartogram that for each area preserves the shape, orientation and centers (or bounding box or something) of each of the sub-areas, changing only their relative size.

There is one more thing that I vaguely remember. I hope. I believe it was described as a shiny interface to somebody else's library, and it had a very short alphanumeric name. j6? d4?  And I think the map I saw was was either of U.S. or Australian states.

Does anyone recognize this from the description? If so, can you point me toward it? It is nice for population characteristics because you can set the area to the population and still have color free to represent your variable of interest.

My most effusive thanks to anyone who can help.

Warmest regards, Andrew Hoerner

messages.body_plain:
Hi John

you are not very specific about the setup you plan to run.
I'm successfully using Apache as reverse proxy to forward requests to shiny-server.
http://myhost/shinyApps/ gets proxied to http://myotherhost:3838/ where shiny is listening.
Another setup would be to run shiny-server on a different port on the same server.

In my experience it works very smoothly, with one exception:
Using shiny-server open source it is difficult to pass information from Apache to the shiny-app. Most header fields are filtered (in particular REMOTE_USER).

Hope this helps.

Henryk

messages.subject: Re: Reading the cookies from Server.r
messages.subject_clean: Reading the cookies from Server.r
messages.body_plain:
My solution involves Apache, mod_headers and mod_rewrite:

My need was to read a session cookie from Shiny server, at page load so, at apache level I extracted it from the headers:

                SetEnvIf Cookie "(^|;\ *)PHPSESSID=([^;\ ]+)" phpsessid=$2

and I added it to the url query string:

                RewriteEngine on
                RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} ^((?!phpsessid=[0-9a-z]+).)*$
                RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} ^.*auth=remote.*$
                RewriteRule ^(.*)$ /$1?phpsessid=%{ENV:phpsessid} [R,L,QSA]

In this way, every time you call the url with the query parameter "auth=remote", you end up with the cookie value on the phpsessid param of the url.
This of course is acceptable if you can afford to have the value on the URL (which is visible). For session cookies this is not the best, but I think is pretty much the same you can obtain with Javascript (where in any case you have to remove the httponly flag!) but with the advantage that the value is available on the server without too many back and forward calls (and at page load time).

messages.body_plain:
Well, it seems like this works:

####################
---
output:
  html_document:
    includes:
      in_header: "tmp.html_"
---

`r 'tmp.html_'`
####################

But this does not:

#####################
---
output:
  html_document:
    includes:
      in_header: "`r 'tmp.html_'`"
---

`r 'tmp.html_'`
#####################

and I get error:

pandoc: `r 'tmp.html_'`: openFile: does not exist (No such file or directory)
Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 1
Execution halted

So it seems like it is not interpreting the inline R code as R.

Best,
Richard

messages.subject: Dynamically Generate Plots in Conditional Tabs using renderUI
messages.subject_clean: Dynamically Generate Plots in Conditional Tabs using renderUI
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I need some help creating dynamic plots that go inside dynamic tabs.  Here's the situation ... I have a data file that contains digital marketing data.  The file has the following pieces of information:  Campaign Name, Channel Name, Page Views, and Visits.  Campaign Names are unique and roll up to one of four different marketing channels.  This will change in the future depending on the data I feed it (for example, I may have six marketing channels in the next file I use), but this will do for troubleshooting purposes.  I want to dynamically create tabs and output for each marketing channel in the file.  I have been able to figure out how to create the tabs, but I'm having a hard time figuring out how to create other types of output (like a plot) to go with each tab.

The tabs were created using renderUI in the following code in the server file:

 output$mytabs = renderUI({
    if(is.null(rawData())){return ()}
    channels = unique(rawData()$Channel)
    myTabs = lapply(channels, tabPanel)
    do.call(tabsetPanel, myTabs)
  })

These were then referenced in the ui file as follows:

   tabPanel("Parameters & Model Fit",
               uiOutput('mytabs')

Ultimately, I'd like to plot Page Views vs Visits for each Marketing Channel.  In my global file, I've created two functions -- one function plots one channel at a time and another function that plots all the channels and saves each one as separate elements within a list.  I'm not sure which one of these will end up being useful.  You'll notice the "Testing" tab in the ui that just shows that my plots actually do generate.

I have tried a number of different things to try and get plots to show up in each tab, but to no avail.  I've attached my code including a snippet to create a csv file that you can use with the upload data function.  Any help would be greatly appreciated!!!

Thanks!
Jess

messages.subject: Re: Dynamically Generate Plots in Conditional Tabs using renderUI
messages.subject_clean: Dynamically Generate Plots in Conditional Tabs using renderUI
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jessica,

I only looked at the second pair of ui/server files. I have a number of suggestions that will hopefully clear up some things.
Why do you have a runApp.R? And why does your server.R source global.R? The contents of ui.R, server.R, and global.R are correct, but you should just do shiny::runApp() to run the app--no need to have your own script to do what Shiny already wants to do for you.
In server.R, you do a lot of `if (is.null(whatever)) return()`. Instead you should use req <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html> in your rawData reactive;, which will let you remove all of those checks.
In your output$mytabs, your lapply is just creating a list of empty tabs. Instead, it should be creating a list of tabs that each contain a plotOutput("plot", i), something like:
myTabs <- lapply(channels, function(ch) {
  tabPanel(ch,
    plotOutput(paste0("plot", i))
  )
})
(you'd need to increment i--hopefully you get the idea).
The createPlots is almost right, but, it shouldn't be a reactive that's called from scatterPlot; it should be an observer instead. I strongly encourage you to watch the Effective Reactive Programming 1 & 2 tutorials here <https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/>.
Also in createPlots, the logic here is fine except that you can get away from the for/local/my_i pattern by using lapply(seq_along(channels), function(i) { ... }) instead.

messages.subject: Re: Resetting action buttons
messages.subject_clean: Resetting action buttons
messages.body_plain:
> > Hi,

I don't know if this discussion is still open but I am facing an issue which could be easily solved if I could turn to zero (or delete from input list) the action button counters.

Mainly my application is a webform where you can add or delete items (through action button).

The values of each part are stored in a reactive values list and the different parts of the application read from the list to display the different parts.

The problem is that my approach to do that was to generate a listener for all the deletion action buttons. The problem with that was that although the button was deleted, the corresponding input value for the action button was still there, which was a problem.

To sum up:

- I hit on button "Create Element" and, let's say a Tab is created, with different elements. Among them, there is a "Delete" button, which deletes that item. This action button has the id "element1_delete"

- I create several other elements and after that I want to delete "element1". I click on the button "Delete" in the "element1" tab.

- I manage to delete it but, as "input$element1_delete" is still there and with a value greater than 0, I cannot re-create the tab "element1" because every time the "deletion listener" is triggered, it will see that "input$element1_delete" is greater than 0 and will take it out from the configuration list.

The only solution I can think of without being able to edit "input$element1_delete" would be to have a register of all the "deletion" buttons, and compare it against that button, which is much more complicated than just "input$element1_delete <- NULL".

In fact, if I could do this, I could delete unnecessary elements inside the input list.

Unfortunately, I cannot share the code so easily but please let me know if I didn't make myself clear and, in that case, I can try to generate a toy example.

Thanks!

Hernan

Hi all,

is it possible within Shiny to expose a global (as in, not per session) POST endpoint, with a configurable handler? My specific use case here is to receive/process Amazon SNS messages, in turn causing a refresh of a data source.

While I can hijack registerDataObj, this requires apriori knowledge of the session token (etc) to construct the actual URL.

Does Shiny at all expose its internal routing handlers?

I would appreciate any guidance you can offer. While I can likely monkey patch my way around, I do not understand the internal routing well enough to know where best to start.

Cheers,

Kadrach

messages.body_plain:
Hi -

You will need to add additional steps to data.new <http://data.new> in order to match multiple criteria (e.g, if "ALL" and "Other" + "Group1" and "Group2" are selected) across multiple columns (Territory and Nob).

One way to do this is to use the %in%  for subsetting data. In the data.new <http://data.new> section, try adding ...

data.new<-reactive({

        #' set a default
        if(is.null(input$Territory) & is.null(input$Nature)){

            return(data) ## simply return the data

        } else {

            data[data$Territory %in% input$Territory & data$Nob %in% input$Nature,]

        }

    })

A quick note:
I added a default action for when no selection is made (i.e., first load)
Hope that helps!

- DCR

messages.subject_clean: Custom routes in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Shiny is amazing but it seems like there are better ways to achieve what you want.

I'd use tried and true frameworks with battle-tested SNS packages, such as Laravel (PHP), Django (Python), or Rails (ruby), to handle the data processing you are describing.

Use a database driver in R to connect to the database driving the above app.

Then make your shiny app do what you need it to.

If you have the knowledge of SNS, tokens, etc. this is going to be far faster than hacking around R/Shiny.

The only reason not to do this would be if some reason you need the above data to be immediately reactive. Even then, I think polling your database in R periodically for data updates would still be easier.

My 2 cents

messages.body_plain:
Think I've found a good reason to implement my first R package. Inspired by Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel's course in Bayesian Statistics, the R package will include functions to be called from an interactive R markdown file to render a shiny app knitted into an html document & publishable to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> .   What I've not seen before is the Rmd's yaml:

output: statsr:::statswithr_lab

seemingly corresponding to a package installed by

devtools::install_github("StatsWithR/statsr")

But, the yaml output parameter doesn't seem to match up with the github package name.

Thanks for clarification on how this works, specifically the relationship between Rmd yaml output parameter and github package name, and any other context for implementing such a package.

I've installed R, R studio, shiny and shiny server, rmarkdown, on an Amazon EC2 instance, and sorted out the firewall.

messages.body_plain:
OK, a couple of things. do.call takes a function (any function), and a list of objects, and calls the function as if those objects were the arguments. For example, do.call(read.csv, list("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) is equivalent to read.csv("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) It's convenient to do this when we're dynamically assembling the arguments to the function, as we're doing now. lapply(channels, tabPanel) is equivalent to calling: list( tabPanel(channel[1]), tabPanel(channel[2]), tabPanel(channel[3]), # and so on... ) So those two lines together amount to: tabsetPanel( tabPanel(channel[1]), tabPanel(channel[2]), tabPanel(channel[3]), # and so on... ) Those tabPanels are empty though, which isn't useful. What you want is a whole bunch of stuff in each tabPanel, right? So instead of calling lapply(channels, tabPanel), you want that second argument not to be tabPanel but a function that generates a tabPanel that contains plotOutputs and whatever else you want to put into each tab. That function will need not only the channel name, but also what position they're at in the list, since you're going to name the plot outputs plot_1, plot_2, etc. One way to do that is to use an mapply instead of lapply: myTabs <- mapply(1:length(channels), channels, FUN = function(i, channel) { tabPanel(channel, plotOutput(paste0("plot_", i)), tableOutput(paste0("table_", i)) ) }) So after the do.call you'll end up with something like tabsetPanel( tabPanel(channel[1], plotOutput("plot_1"), tableOutput("table_1") ), tabPanel(channel[2], plotOutput("plot_2"), tableOutput("table_2") ) ) which is hopefully close to what you want. On Thursday, September 29, 2016 at 9:36:29 AM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > OK, a couple of things. > > do.call takes a function (any function), and a list of objects, and calls the function as if those objects were the arguments. For example, > > do.call(read.csv, list("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) > > is equivalent to > > read.csv("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) > > It's convenient to do this when we're dynamically assembling the arguments to the function, as we're doing now. > > lapply(channels, tabPanel) is equivalent to calling: > > list( > tabPanel(channel[1]), > tabPanel(channel[2]), > tabPanel(channel[3]), > # and so on... > ) > > So those two lines together amount to: > > tabsetPanel( > tabPanel(channel[1]), > tabPanel(channel[2]), > tabPanel(channel[3]), > # and so on... > ) > > Those tabPanels are empty though, which isn't useful. What you want is a whole bunch of stuff in each tabPanel, right? So instead of calling lapply(channels, tabPanel), you want that second argument not to be tabPanel but a function that generates a tabPanel that contains plotOutputs and whatever else you want to put into each tab. > > That function will need not only the channel name, but also what position they're at in the list, since you're going to name the plot outputs plot_1, plot_2, etc. One way to do that is to use an mapply instead of lapply: > > myTabs <- mapply(1:length(channels), channels, FUN = function(i, channel) { > tabPanel(channel, > plotOutput(paste0("plot_", i)), > tableOutput(paste0("table_", i)) > ) > }) > > So after the do.call you'll end up with something like > > tabsetPanel( > tabPanel(channel[1], > plotOutput("plot_1"), > tableOutput("table_1") > ), > tabPanel(channel[2], > plotOutput("plot_2"), > tableOutput("table_2") > ) > ) > > which is hopefully close to what you want. > > On Thu, Sep 29, 2016 at 8:24 AM Jessica Langford wrote: > > Sorry I wasn't very clear. I've looked at the help files and I guess I still don't understand what the following lines of code are doing: > > > > > > myTabs = lapply(channels, tabPanel) > > do.call(tabsetPanel, myTabs) > > > > If I print out the first element in myTabs it looks like this: > > > > [[1]] > >
> > > > I need to add more than just plots to each tab -- For example I need to add 4 inputSliders that are unique to each tab. I thought I could do that by adding more elements to this tag via the tagList() function? Again, sorry if I'm not very clear. Quite new to Shiny :-\ > > > > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, September 29, 2016 at 9:00:00 AM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > > Sorry but I'm not sure what you mean specifically by custom/dynamic tags...? Are you hung up on any of the bullet points I sent, or something a bit different? > > > > > > On Thu, Sep 29, 2016 at 7:51 AM Jessica Langford wrote: > > > > Hi Joe, > > > > > > > > Thanks so much for your reply. I found another solution to fix this specific problem, but I'm realizing that I really need to go back to my original approach. Do you have any good documentation for creating custom/dynamic tags? > > > > > > > > Thanks! > > > > Jess > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Tuesday, September 27, 2016 at 5:27:16 PM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > > > > Hi Jessica, > > > > > > > > > > I only looked at the second pair of ui/server files. I have a number of suggestions that will hopefully clear up some things. > > > > > Why do you have a runApp.R? And why does your server.R source global.R? The contents of ui.R, server.R, and global.R are correct, but you should just do shiny::runApp() to run the app--no need to have your own script to do what Shiny already wants to do for you. > > > > > In server.R, you do a lot of `if (is.null(whatever)) return()`. Instead you should use req in your rawData reactive;, which will let you remove all of those checks. > > > > > In your output$mytabs, your lapply is just creating a list of empty tabs. Instead, it should be creating a list of tabs that each contain a plotOutput("plot", i), something like: > > > > > myTabs <- lapply(channels, function(ch) { > > > > > tabPanel(ch, > > > > > plotOutput(paste0("plot", i)) > > > > > ) > > > > > }) > > > > > (you'd need to increment i--hopefully you get the idea). > > > > > The createPlots is almost right, but, it shouldn't be a reactive that's called from scatterPlot; it should be an observer instead. I strongly encourage you to watch the Effective Reactive Programming 1 & 2 tutorials here . > > > > > Also in createPlots, the logic here is fine except that you can get away from the for/local/my_i pattern by using lapply(seq_along(channels), function(i) { ... }) instead. > > > > > > > > > > On Tue, Sep 27, 2016 at 2:46 PM Jessica Langford wrote: > > > > > > Exciting Update ;) > > > > > > > > > > > > I can now get all four plots to appear on each of the individual channel tabs. messages.body_plain:
I believe the problem is that you're calling stopApp(), which stops the entire application. Because multiple users can be connected to the same application, each with their own session, calling stopApp() will kill all of the sessions.

Your JS code that closes the window should be sufficient to close that user's session.

messages.body_plain:
Great, glad to hear it! On Fri, Sep 30, 2016 at 9:44 AM Jessica Langford wrote: > Joe -- your explanation was perfect and made things so clear. I've been making great progress and I have been able to repeat this solution for other use cases. Thank you so so so much! > > > On Thursday, September 29, 2016 at 9:36:29 AM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > OK, a couple of things. > > > > do.call takes a function (any function), and a list of objects, and calls the function as if those objects were the arguments. For example, > > > > do.call(read.csv, list("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) > > > > is equivalent to > > > > read.csv("data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) > > > > It's convenient to do this when we're dynamically assembling the arguments to the function, as we're doing now. > > > > lapply(channels, tabPanel) is equivalent to calling: > > > > list( > > tabPanel(channel[1]), > > tabPanel(channel[2]), > > tabPanel(channel[3]), > > # and so on... > > ) > > > > So those two lines together amount to: > > > > tabsetPanel( > > tabPanel(channel[1]), > > tabPanel(channel[2]), > > tabPanel(channel[3]), > > # and so on... > > ) > > > > Those tabPanels are empty though, which isn't useful. What you want is a whole bunch of stuff in each tabPanel, right? So instead of calling lapply(channels, tabPanel), you want that second argument not to be tabPanel but a function that generates a tabPanel that contains plotOutputs and whatever else you want to put into each tab. > > > > That function will need not only the channel name, but also what position they're at in the list, since you're going to name the plot outputs plot_1, plot_2, etc. One way to do that is to use an mapply instead of lapply: > > > > myTabs <- mapply(1:length(channels), channels, FUN = function(i, channel) { > > tabPanel(channel, > > plotOutput(paste0("plot_", i)), > > tableOutput(paste0("table_", i)) > > ) > > }) > > > > So after the do.call you'll end up with something like > > > > tabsetPanel( > > tabPanel(channel[1], > > plotOutput("plot_1"), > > tableOutput("table_1") > > ), > > tabPanel(channel[2], > > plotOutput("plot_2"), > > tableOutput("table_2") > > ) > > ) > > > > which is hopefully close to what you want. > > > > On Thu, Sep 29, 2016 at 8:24 AM Jessica Langford wrote: > > > Sorry I wasn't very clear. I've looked at the help files and I guess I still don't understand what the following lines of code are doing: > > > > > > > > > myTabs = lapply(channels, tabPanel) > > > do.call(tabsetPanel, myTabs) > > > > > > If I print out the first element in myTabs it looks like this: > > > > > > [[1]] > > >
> > > > > > I need to add more than just plots to each tab -- For example I need to add 4 inputSliders that are unique to each tab. I thought I could do that by adding more elements to this tag via the tagList() function? Again, sorry if I'm not very clear. Quite new to Shiny :-\ > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, September 29, 2016 at 9:00:00 AM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > > > Sorry but I'm not sure what you mean specifically by custom/dynamic tags...? Are you hung up on any of the bullet points I sent, or something a bit different? > > > > > > > > On Thu, Sep 29, 2016 at 7:51 AM Jessica Langford wrote: > > > > > Hi Joe, > > > > > > > > > > Thanks so much for your reply. I found another solution to fix this specific problem, but I'm realizing that I really need to go back to my original approach. Do you have any good documentation for creating custom/dynamic tags? > > > > > > > > > > Thanks! > > > > > Jess > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Tuesday, September 27, 2016 at 5:27:16 PM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > > > > > Hi Jessica, > > > > > > > > > > > > I only looked at the second pair of ui/server files. I have a number of suggestions that will hopefully clear up some things. > > > > > > Why do you have a runApp.R? And why does your server.R source global.R? The contents of ui.R, server.R, and global.R are correct, but you should just do shiny::runApp() to run the app--no need to have your own script to do what Shiny already wants to do for you. > > > > > > In server.R, you do a lot of `if (is.null(whatever)) return()`. Instead you should use req in your rawData reactive;, which will let you remove all of those checks. > > > > > > In your output$mytabs, your lapply is just creating a list of empty tabs. Instead, it should be creating a list of tabs that each contain a plotOutput("plot", i), something like: > > > > > > myTabs <- lapply(channels, function(ch) { > > > > > > tabPanel(ch, > > > > > > plotOutput(paste0("plot", i)) > > > > > > ) > > > > > > }) > > > > > > (you'd need to increment i--hopefully you get the idea). > > > > > > The createPlots is almost right, but, it shouldn't be a reactive that's called from scatterPlot; it should be an observer instead. I strongly encourage you to watch the Effective Reactive Programming 1 & 2 tutorials here . > > > > > > Also in createPlots, the logic here is fine except that you can get away from the for/local/my_i pattern by using lapply(seq_along(channels), function(i) { ... }) instead. > > > > > > > > > > > > On Tue, Sep 27, 2016 at 2:46 PM Jessica Langford wrote: > > > > > > > Exciting Update ;) > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I can now get all four plots to appear on each of the individual channel tabs. Still having trouble getting one plot to show up on a corresponding channel tab.
